clue.text: Plane, provided with external encouragement, will become interesting

parts.note: the Comet was the de Havilland jet airliner

indicators.note: the encouragement is placed on the outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: olé is the Spanish cry of encouragement heard at bullfights
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: An aircraft, cheered on from outside, is about to get exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with external' wraps the encouragement round 'provided'; 'will' is a link, so the definition is the bare infinitive.
explanation.definitionFit: To come alive figuratively is to grow lively and engaging, an idiom for becoming interesting.

clue.text: Watch out for the hole

definitions.meaning: ...! is Latin for 'beware', old British schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the public-school warning cry, the other a hollow in a hillside.

clue.text: Parents love son being embraced by girl — one enjoying humiliation

parts.note: mas are mothers, plural of ma
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the son sits held inside the girl

parts.note: a chit is a pert young girl

explanation.surface: A family scene ends with someone who relishes being humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being embraced by' puts S inside CHIT to give CHIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes pleasure in pain or degradation is the standard sense of this word.

clue.text: Confectionery providing pleasure in Ankara

definitions.meaning: a gel sweet cut in cubes and dusted with sugar
read literally, joy felt in the capital of Turkey

explanation.definitionFit: The sweet's name read word by word is enjoyment of a Turkish kind, Ankara being Turkey's capital.

clue.text: Support friend, keeping within the law

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Backing a mate while staying on the right side of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting lawfully means acting within what statute permits, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Flower appearing wild over most of oriental country once

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: wild animals are free, not captive

indicators.note: the last letter of the country name is dropped

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A bloom seems to grow untamed across much of old Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant flowering plant of the iris family.

clue.text: Part of the world to the west is crossed by drivers

indicators.note: the drivers' letters straddle the other piece

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A region to the west has motorists criss-crossing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' reads the little word right to left, and 'is crossed by' sets it inside the drivers' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, one of the great divisions of the globe.

clue.text: Cast left without protection? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece goes without the other, so it is removed
swaps the roles in the clue's phrase: protection loses left rather than left losing protection

parts.note: a shield gives protection

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out undefended, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, L would lose SHIELD; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so SHIELD loses L.
explanation.definitionFit: Shied is the past tense of shy, to throw, so it means flung or cast.

clue.text: Motoring's a strange occupation for expert on land

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something strange is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: its letters including the S are used

explanation.surface: Driving would be an odd line of work for a soil specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Motoring's' is fodder here, and 'occupation for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist is a scientist of soil management and crop production, an expert on farmland.

clue.text: A part of geese I'd fancy

definitions.text: A part of geese I'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or rework, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: its fourteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A diner picks the bit of the goose they would like to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the dish is literally a part of geese that many fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: The delicacy is made from the fattened liver of a goose, a part of geese.

clue.text: Sunshade — it's been dropped by tourist

indicators.note: the tourist's word has lost these letters

parts.note: a tourist is a visitor
the word it, with 's meaning has

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker has lost their sun hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been dropped by' takes IT out of VISITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a peak or shield worn to keep sun from the eyes.

clue.text: Gardener I retrained as a guard

indicators.note: trained afresh suggests the letters reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horticulturist has been re-schooled for sentry duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment, so a grenadier is a guardsman.

clue.text: Bill suffering most in police college with sinew

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: the suffering piece goes inside the college

parts.note: Hendon is the Metropolitan Police training college in London
illest is the superlative of ill

explanation.surface: An account of the sickest cadet at a police academy with a pulled muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the superlative after the college's first letter; 'with' is a link. Hendon in north London houses the Metropolitan Police training college.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel cord is a tendon, a type of sinew linking calf muscle to bone.

clue.text: Fondness for 3 and the like displayed by pet — canine, perhaps

parts.note: sweet is an endearment like pet or darling
a canine is one kind of tooth

explanation.surface: A dog shows a liking for treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to 3-down, the Turkish sweet; 'displayed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a liking for sugary things is the idiom; 3-down is one such sweet.

clue.text: With several scores being substantial

parts.note: four twenties, a score being twenty

explanation.surface: A tally of many twenties counts as significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighty means heavy or important, a synonym for substantial.

clue.text: Hazel produces this nut — Emma is different

indicators.note: being different means the letters take another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hazel tree bears a nut, but Emma has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name beside Emma, but it is the tree; 'nut' is fodder, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amentum is a catkin, the dangling flower spike a hazel bears.

clue.text: Catch this and you're bust

parts.note: the number completes the title of Joseph Heller's Catch novel, and in pontoon going over twenty-one means bust

explanation.definitionFit: In card games of twenty-one, such a total exceeds the limit; it also follows Heller's 'Catch-'.

clue.text: Inordinate amount of radiation found after a time in river

indicators.note: the time and radiation pieces go inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the radiation piece comes after the time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a rem is a unit of radiation dose

explanation.surface: Excessive radiation detected in a river after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TREM inside EXE; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, as does extreme.

clue.text: Subject of Eastern dance coming up about noon

indicators.note: the reversed dance wraps round the noon letter
in a down clue, coming up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: valse is the French word for waltz

explanation.surface: The topic of an Oriental dance rising around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns VALSE into ESLAV, and 'about' puts N inside after its first E; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To subject a people is to subjugate or make slaves of them; a verb sense.

clue.text: They link equally sunny places — one's. old half of Finnish capital

parts.note: one is I, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: the first four of the capital's eight letters

parts.note: Helsinki is the capital of Finland

explanation.surface: Lines joining sunny places, part of an old Finnish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An isohel is a line on a map joining places with equal hours of sunshine.

clue.text: Not believing lad finally moves up in area of cricket ground

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter shifts higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: the infield is the part of a cricket field near the pitch
the last letter of lad, named by 'lad finally'

explanation.surface: A doubting boy eventually advances on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lad finally' names D, the last letter of lad, which 'moves up' shifts in INFIELD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is an unbeliever, so the word can mean not believing in a faith.

clue.text: A nail in the coffin supplied by Judas?

definitions.meaning: Judas betrayed Jesus with a kiss, which led to his death

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an act that ensures ruin, and literally describes Judas's fatal kiss in Gethsemane.

clue.text: Build up

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to construct; as an adjective it means upright.

clue.text: Go and fix photograph

definitions.meaning: an attempt, as in have a go
a dose of a drug, an injection
a picture taken with a camera

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an attempt, an injection of a drug, and a snapped picture.

clue.text: Caught up crossing river

indicators.note: the up piece spans across the river letter

parts.note: overhead means up above

explanation.surface: Snagged high above while crossing a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, often by chance, so caught means heard by accident.

clue.text: Strain to hear unfortunate person

indicators.note: the word is said out loud, with its silent W lost

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy or unlucky person

explanation.surface: It is a strain to listen to a poor soul.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit.

clue.text: Emotion that England has inspired

indicators.note: breathed in, so taken inside the words

explanation.surface: A feeling the English nation has stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; the letters run across 'that England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is a strong emotion of loathing.

clue.text: Cast spell on the water separating lovers

indicators.note: cast as in throwing about, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: its ten letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A sorcerer bewitches the sea that keeps sweethearts apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend Leander swam this strait nightly to his lover Hero, until he drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dardanelles strait divided Hero and Leander, the classical lovers.
